text:
alex: quick RFC follow-up — I want to propose we tighten the onboarding contract for token ownership between gateway and metering.
maria: curious — what's the main pain we're solving? seems related to late credits and complex provenance.
john: yep. current flow has gateway emit a provisional `token_event` and metering finalizes ownership later. that split is causing duplicates and reconciliation headaches.
alex: exactly. idea: emit a single authoritative `ownership_intent` event at request completion with these fields: `token_id`, `owner_id` (nullable), `seq_id`, `finalized` (bool), `origin` (gateway/dedicated). then metering either accepts as authoritative or emits a `correction` event.
devon: sounds simpler. how do we handle cases where gateway can't decide owner immediately (eg. cached account resolution)?
alex: two options: 1) gateway holds request until resolution and emits authoritative event; 2) gateway emits `ownership_intent` with `finalized=false` and a mandated `finalization_deadline` and a stable `seq_id` so later finalize can correlate.
maria: option 2 reduces tail latency at gateway but pushes complexity to metering for idempotent finalization. is that acceptable?
john: metering already has idempotent reducer patterns. we can require finalizers to include `finalizer_id` + `seq_id` and apply compare-and-set semantics. adds a bit of state in the store but avoids blocking the gateway.
alex: I prefer option 2 for latency. we'd add these invariants: finalizer must include `seq_id`, `prev_state_hash` (optional) and `finalized=true`. metering will only apply a finalize if seq greater or prev_state_hash matches.
devon: audit implications: we need to keep lineage for `provisional` -> `finalized` transitions for compliance. store both events in the audit log and tag the final one as canonical.
infra-bot: deploy note: adding `finalization_deadline` requires schema bump v2.3 and kafka topic retention considerations. will need migration doc.
maria: also need to think about routing: should provisional events be routed to a cheap hot lane and finalizes to the canonical accounting shard?
john: yes. provisional -> low-cost stream for near-real-time dashboards, finalizes -> canonical metering pipeline (stronger consistency) for billing.
alex: rollback strategy: if a finalize never arrives by deadline, metering should 1) mark as `unclaimed` and 2) kick a small re-resolve job + emit an `audit_unfinalized` event to ops.
devon: add a health metric: count of `unfinalized` past deadline per project — triggers SRE paging if spike.
maria: one more: backwards compatibility — older gateways will emit only `provisional` events. plan: metering accepts them and treats them as `finalized=false`; finalizers can come later. include a migration flag to validate seq_id presence.
alex: next steps: I'll draft a slim RFC with schema example and reconciliation pseudocode. want volunteers to review the model and the idempotency semantics.
john: I can review the idempotency + reducer code paths.
devon: I'll vet the alerting and cost route changes.
maria: I'll take the audit log retention + compliance language.
alex: thanks all. I'll post the RFC link in this thread when done. :thumbsup:
